rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. At-fault reasons include failure to pay rent, failure to cure a lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant at the end of the lease term. No-fault reasons include owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, a government order to vacate, a HUD sale, residential hotel conversion or demolition, and conversion to affordable housing; for no-fault evictions the owner may have to pay relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties containing only one single-family dwelling. It applies to a tenancy once the tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, the owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers for substance abuse, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. Tenants evicted for at-fault reasons are not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction_text: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: amount owed higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR)
rules.coverage_text: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR). The FMR depends on the bedroom size of the rental unit.

rules.title: Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: within three (3) business days of service
rules.coverage_text: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower. The page states the maximum allowable increase from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 is 8.9%.
rules.key_value: 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis, excluding the listed exemptions.
